origin.socialStatus: Host; keeper of the door and of the book of stakes
origin.profession: Former guard and clerk; no one knows the details

appearance.face: Invisible. The face is hidden in the shadow of the hood
appearance.clothing: A heavy grey hooded cloak, a big old key around the neck, leather gloves
appearance.gestures: Always stands by the door; does not move until someone breaks a rule
appearance.voice: A quiet, flat, muffled voice; speaks only when necessary
appearance.firstImpression: A silent, unsettling figure everyone forgets until it speaks
appearance.artistNotes: The key around the neck opens the inn's door. Carries a thick book in which every stake and every promise at the table is written down.

backstory.biography: No one knows much about the Keeper. They say he was a guard, then a court clerk, and that he left both because people break rules too easily. He does not joke, does not threaten, and does not explain the rules more than necessary. With him there are no accidental pardons.
backstory.whyHere: He keeps the door, the order and the book of stakes. He believes the table means something only if the rules apply to everyone.
backstory.secret: Who he was before. And whether he himself ever broke a rule.

psychology.weakness: Makes no exceptions even when he should
psychology.moralLimits: Applies the rules to everyone, himself included

behavior.deception: Does not use it. Points it out if it breaks a rule
behavior.debts: Writes them down and collects them
behavior.whenAttacks: Only when a rule is broken or a debt unpaid
behavior.strategyChange: Only a new rule announced at the start of the evening

motives.hiddenGoal: For every stake to be paid
motives.personalReason: The belief that order matters more than people

mechanics.strangeness: His book records promises that have not been spoken yet.
mechanics.temptation: Makes no exceptions even when he should

authorNotes.distinctive: The faceless judge: quiet, relentless, fair.
authorNotes.tunable: How strict he is about small offences.

host.presentation: As the keeper of the door
host.trueNature: A dry, pedantic man for whom order is everything
host.punishment: Announces the offence aloud and demands it be put right
host.hostingStyle: Stands by the door, silent, and steps in only when a rule is broken. Announces penalties in a word or two.
host.sampleOffers: Offers no temptations. Only the settling of a debt: "The debt can be paid now. Or later, with interest."
host.trueStory: Once he lost everything because someone broke their word. Since then he keeps the words of others.
host.changedRule: Dawn announces only the deaths — broken amulets and the heaviest purse stay secret.

lines.text: The doors are open. The debts are not.
The promise is broken. The debt is recorded.
The stake is accepted. So are the consequences.
Your name is already in the book.
The Keeper. I write. I remember.
The rules apply from this moment.
Your role is recorded. It cannot be changed.

tells.description: Stands by the door and does not move
Moves only when someone breaks a rule
